items.original_title: FinancialJuice: ING: “Bessent Put” Supports Risk Assets and Weighs on the Dollar

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: ING: “Bessent Put” Supports Risk Assets and Weighs on the Dollar
evidence.snippet: The US Treasury’s decision to increase long-end buybacks has been welcomed as a sign that officials are becoming more willing to lean against disorderly rises in longer-dated yields. The move does not solve the underlying fiscal problem, but it reduces one of the main threats to risk assets and has helped pull long yields lower, lift equities and weaken the dollar, particularly against higher-beta currencies. The July FOMC minutes also failed to deliver a strongly hawkish message, with short-dated yields falling after the release. That combination leaves markets in a more “risk-on, dollar-off” environment, supportive of carry trades and EMFX. If risk assets extend the move, the dollar could continue to drift lower.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Deutsche Bank on Treasury Buyback Announcement

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Deutsche Bank on Treasury Buyback Announcement
evidence.snippet: Markets recovered yesterday after the US Treasury unexpectedly announced it would at least double the size of buyback operations for longer-dated Treasuries. The move drove the 30-year yield down 9.2bps to 5.19%, its biggest decline since June, while the yield curve flattened sharply. The increased buybacks will cover 10-30 year maturities, with the maximum size per operation rising from $2bn to at least $4bn from September 9 through November 4. Although the amounts are small relative to the overall Treasury market, the announcement signalled a willingness to support the long end after 30-year yields recently reached their highest since 2007. The move also had broader cross-asset effects: gold surged 4.18%, its biggest gain since March, while the dollar index fell 0.83% to a three-month low as investors considered the implications for financial repression and long-term rates.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: ING: The EUR

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: ING: The EUR
evidence.snippet: EUR/USD broke higher yesterday on the US Treasury news, which could usher in a slightly more encouraging, or at least stable, investment environment. Ever-higher natural gas prices in Europe remain a worry, but investors are thinking about another bearish dollar leg emerging, with EUR/USD playing its part. Behind the scenes, foreigners are also buying a lot of eurozone debt and equities. Data released by the European Central Bank yesterday showed that foreigners have bought around €l.ltr of eurozone securities over the last 12 months. And June saw the largest ever monthly purchases of debt at €200bn. Thus, the bullish euro narrative of diversification away from the US remains present. Yesterday's US intervention has brought EUR/USD close to our end-September target of 1.17. Resistance at 1.1700 may be a tough nut to crack in the short term, but if so, 1.1790 beckons. Support may be found as close as 1.1650/60. Also, a reminder that we consider European asset managers underhedaed on their US investments.
